judged_text: deleteEvent has the same tautological find: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` evaluates the find only when externalCalendarId is falsy, guaranteeing undefined. Cancelling a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId now calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId, so the remote event is never deleted and orphaned Google Calendar events accumulate.

record.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent has the same tautological find: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` evaluates the find only when externalCalendarId is falsy, guaranteeing undefined. Cancelling a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId now calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId, so the remote event is never deleted and orphaned Google Calendar events accumulate.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar id as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Since the `find` predicate compares against the (falsy) `externalCalendarId`, it will not select the event’s destination calendar and will typically return `undefined`. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (when it was a single object). This regression can cause deletes/updates to target `undefined`/default (`primary`) rather than the actual destination calendar, leaving remote events undeleted (or attempting deletion in the wrong calendar).
